assertions.assertion: Turn 2 is read as a divergence: the agent shifts up and records the divergence. Any earlier claim that the new design makes wrong is replaced by a new claim, not edited; an earlier outcome claim that still holds may stay.
assertions.evidence: The agent treated turn 2 as just "a new change request". Its delivery says "KB: No KB" and "Triggers: none fired. One request, no divergence", so it neither shifted up nor recorded a divergence or any claim.

assertions.assertion: The turn-1 outcome (a reader who opted out gets no newsletter, whatever the capitals or surrounding spaces of the address in either file, and new opt-outs typed that way too) is kept as a claim and checked again under the hashed opt-out list, against the converted existing rows and not only against a newly added opt-out.
assertions.evidence: The agent did re-run the earlier test, test_opt_out_ignores_case_and_spaces, which calls recipients() on the real data, and it checked that "None of the 9 matches an opt-out hash" against the converted file. But the outcome was never kept as a claim: the agent said "No KB" and recorded no claims, so the 'kept as a claim' part is not met.

assertions.assertion: The delivery does not claim that the hashed opt-out list skips the same readers as before, or that the turn-1 fix still holds, without a check that runs the send against the converted file with addresses that differ in capitals or spaces between the two files.
assertions.evidence: The claim "The Friday fix still works" is backed by a check. The turn-1 test calls recipients() on the converted optouts.csv and asserts that maria.k, dev.patel and jo.bauer are excluded, and all 7 tests pass. Those three addresses differ in capitals or spaces between the two files. The agent also reported that, on the real data, none of the 9 remaining readers matches an opt-out hash.
